name: Rudolf Steiner
role: Austrian philosopher, esotericist and founder of anthroposophy (1861-1925)
summary: Founder of anthroposophy who, after the First World War, advocated 'social threefolding': a free self-administered cultural and educational sphere, a democratic rights-state limited to equal legal matters, and an economy run by voluntary associations of producers, traders and consumers rather than by the state or by capital for profit. He rejected both state socialism and unregulated capitalism, favoured free trade as an ideal, and argued from a philosophy of ethical individualism that moral action rests on individual intuition rather than duty or general norms.

notes: Evidence is concentrated in his 1919-20 social writings (Threefold Commonwealth, GA 24 articles) and the Philosophy of Freedom; the library holds the Gutenberg text of the first and Philosophy of Freedom in scratchpad/sources/rudolf-steiner/. Themes searched: economy (property, capital, wages, inheritance, credit, land, trade), government (democracy, franchise, state limits, courts, parliaments), world (war guilt, Wilson, nationalities, international economy), education and religion, ethics. Not searched in primary texts: his lectures on race, Jews, gender, health and agriculture, which are outside the political writings; Wikipedia and a blocked Cornell PDF were not used. Gender, family, immigration, security, environment, technology and most modern statements are null as he did not address them in the sources read.
